name: f = x^rho L(x) with L slowly varying
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.isRegularlyVarying_iff_exists_isSlowlyVarying {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ : ℝ} :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ ↔
    ∃ L, ExtremeValueTheory.IsSlowlyVarying L ∧ ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, f x = x ^ ρ * L x
scope_note: The equality holds eventually. Measurability is a separate hypothesis throughout the library, not part of the definition.

name: Uniform convergence theorem, monotone case
scope_note: Assumes f monotone or antitone on some [a, infinity). The theorem for measurable f is uct-measurable.

name: Uniform convergence theorem
scope_note: Measurable f on all of R, which is the book's hypothesis up to changing f far out.

name: Potter bounds, monotone case
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.potter_bound {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ : ℝ}
  (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ) {a : ℝ}
  (hmono : MonotoneOn f (Set.Ici a) ∨ AntitoneOn f (Set.Ici a)) {δ A : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ)
  (hA : 1 < A) :
  ∃ x₀,
    0 < x₀ ∧
      (∀ x ≥ x₀, 0 < f x) ∧
        ∀ x ≥ x₀, ∀ y ≥ x₀, f y / f x ≤ A * max ((y / x) ^ (ρ + δ)) ((y / x) ^ (ρ - δ))
scope_note: Assumes f eventually monotone or antitone, and gives only the upper bound. The general form is potter-measurable.

name: Potter bounds, two-sided
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.potter_bounds_of_measurable {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ : ℝ}
  (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ) (hm : Measurable f) {δ A : ℝ} (hδ : 0 < δ)
  (hA : 1 < A) :
  ∃ x₀,
    0 < x₀ ∧
      (∀ x ≥ x₀, 0 < f x) ∧
        ∀ x ≥ x₀,
          ∀ y ≥ x₀,
            A⁻¹ * min ((y / x) ^ (ρ + δ)) ((y / x) ^ (ρ - δ)) ≤ f y / f x ∧
              f y / f x ≤ A * max ((y / x) ^ (ρ + δ)) ((y / x) ^ (ρ - δ))
scope_note: Measurable f; adds the matching lower bound and positivity of f on [x0, infinity).

name: Karamata's representation theorem
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.isSlowlyVarying_iff_exists_representation {L : ℝ → ℝ} (hm : Measurable L) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsSlowlyVarying L ↔
    ∃ a,
      0 < a ∧
        ∃ c ε,
          Measurable c ∧
            Measurable ε ∧
              (∃ c₀, 0 < c₀ ∧ Filter.Tendsto c Filter.atTop (nhds c₀)) ∧
                Filter.Tendsto ε Filter.atTop (nhds 0) ∧
                  (∀ x ≥ a, IntervalIntegrable (fun t => ε t / t) MeasureTheory.volume a x) ∧
                    ∀ x ≥ a, L x = c x * Real.exp (∫ (t : ℝ) in a..x, ε t / t)
scope_note: Measurability of L is a hypothesis on both sides, and interval integrability of eps(t)/t is stated so the integral is not a junk value.

name: Karamata's tail-integral theorem, antitone case
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendsto_integral_Ioi_div {F : ℝ → ℝ} {α : ℝ} (hF : Antitone F)
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying F (-α)) (hα : 1 < α) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi x, F t) / (x * F x)) Filter.atTop
    (nhds (1 / (α - 1)))
scope_note: Assumes F antitone on all of R, stronger than local boundedness. The measurable version is karamata-tail.

name: Karamata's tail-integral theorem
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendsto_integral_Ioi_div_of_measurable {F : ℝ → ℝ} {α : ℝ}
  (hm : Measurable F) (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying F (-α)) (hα : 1 < α) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi x, F t) / (x * F x)) Filter.atTop
    (nhds (1 / (α - 1)))
scope_note: Measurable F, no monotonicity. Direct half only; the converse is karamata-converse.

name: Karamata's theorem, converse half, tail integrals
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.of_tendsto_mul_div_integral_Ioi_of_pos {F : ℝ → ℝ} {α : ℝ}
  (hpos : ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, 0 < F x) (hα : 1 < α)
  (h :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun x => x * F x / ∫ (t : ℝ) in Set.Ioi x, F t) Filter.atTop (nhds (α - 1))) :
  ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying F (-α)
scope_note: The tail case with weight sigma = 0. Assumes only eventual positivity. The weighted form is of_tendsto_rpow_mul_div_integral_Ioi, the rho > -1 case of_tendsto_mul_div_integral. The book's statement was recalled, not checked.

name: Karamata's theorem for integrals over [a, x]
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying.tendsto_integral_interval_div {f : ℝ → ℝ} {ρ a : ℝ}
  (hf : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying f ρ) (hm : Measurable f) (hρ : -1 < ρ)
  (hint : ∀ x ≥ a, IntervalIntegrable f MeasureTheory.volume a x) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (∫ (t : ℝ) in a..x, f t) / (x * f x)) Filter.atTop (nhds (1 / (ρ + 1)))
scope_note: Any lower limit a, with integrability on [a, x]. Assumes f Borel measurable on all of R; tendsto_integral_div_of_measurableNearTop assumes it only near infinity.

name: Breiman's lemma
statement:
ExtremeValueTheory.tendsto_measure_mul_div_measure.{u_1} {Ω : Type u_1} [MeasurableSpace Ω]
  {P : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω} [MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure P] {X Y : Ω → ℝ}
  (hX : Measurable X) (hY : Measurable Y) (hXY : ProbabilityTheory.IndepFun X Y P)
  (hY0 : ∀ᵐ (ω : Ω) ∂P, 0 ≤ Y ω) {α ε : ℝ} (hα : 0 < α) (hε : 0 < ε)
  (hRV : ExtremeValueTheory.IsRegularlyVarying (fun x => (P {ω | x < X ω}).toReal) (-α))
  (hmom : MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun ω => Y ω ^ (α + ε)) P) :
  Filter.Tendsto (fun x => (P {ω | x < X ω * Y ω}).toReal / (P {ω | x < X ω}).toReal) Filter.atTop
    (nhds (∫ (ω : Ω), Y ω ^ α ∂P))
scope_note: No sign condition on X, as in the reference. Scalar X and Y only.
